A tier is a grouping VIEW (extraction emits `contains`), distinct from the canonical placement edge `hosted_on` - the resolver de-dupes so a resource in both is not double-counted.

replicas.description: Number of replicas for services in this tier.

environment.description: A deployment environment as a first-class, referenceable entity (v2.7.7, ENV###). Environments are a binding dimension (production/staging/dr/…) - each carries its own target scope, credentials, and parameter overlay. Substrate-neutral: cloud, on-premise, and hybrid are equally expressible.

id.description: Typed environment id (ENV###). Referenced by bindings (BND###) and per-environment config.

name.description: Human-readable environment name (e.g. production, staging, dr-site).

env_class.description: Environment class. Orthogonal to substrate - a `dr` environment may be cloud OR on-prem.

substrate.description: Where this environment physically runs. Makes the cloud-versus-on-prem split legible for impact and cost analysis.

provider.description: Optional platform provider - free-text so on-prem/private-cloud fit: azure, aws, gcp, vmware, openstack, bare-metal, k8s, … A hybrid environment may carry a compound value (e.g. 'azure+vmware').

target_scope.description: The deployment partition/boundary this environment maps into (substrate-neutral).

credential_scope.description: Optional logical credential/identity scope (e.g. a subscription, a service account, an AD domain). A reference/label, never a secret value.

param_overlay.description: Optional per-environment parameter overlay applied to bindings (carried; not yet consumed).

target_scope.description: The deployment partition an environment targets. Two additive forms (v2.7.7): the legacy INLINE `{kind, name}` object OR a REFERENCE `{ ref: DSC### }` to a first-class DeploymentScope. Substrate-neutral: cloud (account/subscription/project/resource_group/region/availability_zone), kubernetes (cluster/namespace), and on-premise (datacenter/site/rack/host_pool/vlan) all coexist.

target_scope_inline.description: Inline substrate-neutral scope partition ({kind, name}). The v2.7.7 form promotes this to a reference (target_scope_ref -> DSC###) when the scope is modelled as a first-class DeploymentScope.

kind.description: Partition type across substrates. Cloud, k8s, and on-prem scopes are all first-class.

name.description: Optional concrete scope name/identifier (e.g. a subscription id, an AWS account, a datacenter code 'dc-1'). A reference/label, not a secret.

target_scope_ref.description: Reference form (v2.7.7): point an environment's target scope at a first-class DeploymentScope (DSC###) instead of inlining {kind, name}. Additive - the inline form stays valid.

scope_kind.description: Deployment partition type across substrates (substrate-neutral): cloud (account/subscription/project/resource_group/region/availability_zone), kubernetes (cluster/namespace), on-premise (datacenter/site/rack/host_pool/vlan). The single source shared by `target_scope` (inline) and `deployment_scope.kind`.

deployment_scope.description: A deployment scope (DSC###, v2.7.7) - a substrate-neutral management / lifecycle / ownership / billing partition. Generalizes an Azure Resource Group or Subscription, an AWS Account / OU, a GCP Project / Folder, a Kubernetes Cluster / Namespace, or an on-prem Datacenter / host-pool. Scopes nest via `parent` (subscription -> resource- group). A resource joins a scope via `resource.scope_ref`. Distinct from TOSCA `hosted_on` (runtime placement): a DB may be `scope_ref` its own resource-group yet `hosted_on` a shared pool (the RG-vs-pool distinction).

id.description: Typed scope identifier (DSC###). Matches the reference fields that point at it (`parent`, `resource.scope_ref`, `environment.target_scope.ref`).

name.description: Human-readable scope name (e.g. the 'prod' subscription, the 'Accounting' resource-group).

kind.description: Partition type (subscription / resource_group / account / project / cluster / namespace / datacenter / host_pool / ...).

parent.description: Optional parent scope (DSC###) - builds the hierarchy (a resource_group's parent subscription; a namespace's parent cluster). A top-tier scope (subscription/account/project/cluster/datacenter) omits it.

substrate.description: Optional substrate this scope lives on. When present it is the MOST authoritative substrate signal for member resources - stronger than transitive `hosted_on` walking or the `platform.name` heuristic.

provider.description: Optional platform provider (free-text so on-prem fits): azure, aws, gcp, vmware, openstack, k8s, ...

owner.description: Optional ownership (vendor / team / contact) for this scope.

region.description: Optional default region/location for resources in this scope (e.g. westeurope, eu-west-1).

description.description: Detailed description of this scope's purpose and what it contains.

properties.description: Open metadata bag for scope-level custom attributes.

infra_relation_edge.description: A typed inter-resource relation (TOSCA vocabulary). `hosted_on` is the canonical placement edge; `connects_to`/`depends_on` may carry attribute-level output refs; `depends_on` is the ordering-only fallback. A `network-link` resource's connects_to/routes_to targets may sit in a different environment/substrate (the hybrid boundary). `routes_to` may also name a service (SVC###): the resource forwards requests to it, as a bought API gateway or load balancer does for the services behind it. Every other verb names a resource.

type.description: TOSCA relation verb: hosted_on / connects_to / depends_on / attaches_to / routes_to.

target.description: The target: a resource (IR###) for every verb, or a service (SVC###) for `routes_to` only, named by its exact declared id. An id that names nothing declared is a cross-reference error. A resource target may be in another environment/substrate (hybrid interconnect). A resource type (RT###) or a third-party package (PKG###) is never a target.

outputs.description: Optional attribute-level outputs of the target this resource consumes - e.g. host, port, connection-string. Makes connects_to/depends_on wiring explicit for impact analysis. Only a resource target has outputs: a relation whose target is a service carries no `outputs`, not even an empty list.

description.description: Optional human note on this edge (e.g. 'reads via read-replica').

iac_refs.description: Traceability links from a resource to its Infrastructure-as-Code - the infra analogue of code_refs. Spans cloud provisioners AND on-prem config-management so on-prem IaC is first-class.

iac_ref.description: A single Infrastructure-as-Code reference: which system defines the resource, and where.

system.description: The IaC system. Cloud provisioners (terraform/opentofu/bicep/arm/cloudformation/pulumi/crossplane) and on-prem config-management (ansible/puppet/chef/saltstack) plus kubernetes/helm are all first-class.

locator.description: Where the resource is defined in that system (e.g. module path, `file:resource` address, Ansible role, Helm chart).

role.description: Optional role of this reference (e.g. 'defines', 'configures', 'deploys'). 'planned' means the locator is where the resource is to be defined and it is not defined there yet; 'gap' means the locator shows the resource is absent where it would be expected. Neither is evidence that the resource is implemented.

lifecycle.description: Optional lifecycle/protection posture for a resource (architect-altitude). Substrate-neutral: 'protected' means change-guarded whether cloud or on-prem.

create_before_destroy.description: Replacements create the new instance before destroying the old.

retain_on_delete.description: Retain the underlying resource when the model entity is removed.

binding.description: Resolves (resource-type × environment) → a concrete implementation: which platform module realizes the type in that environment, with a pinned version and params. The same neutral type binds differently per environment - an azure module in a `cloud` ENV, an on-prem module in an `on-prem` ENV (hybrid = two bindings). Resolution is MOST-SPECIFIC-MATCH: a binding with `need_ref` beats one matching by `type_ref` alone; a binding scoped to an `environment_ref` beats an environment-agnostic default.

type_ref.description: The resource TYPE (RT###) this binding realizes. Pair with `environment_ref` for a (type × env) rule.

need_ref.description: Optional reference to a service `need` id (the free-string need `id`) this binding satisfies - more specific than binding-by-type. Most-specific-match: a `need_ref` binding wins over a `type_ref`-only binding for the same environment.

environment_ref.description: The environment (ENV###) this binding applies to. Omit for an environment-agnostic default (least specific).

resource_ref.description: Optional concrete resource (IR###) this binding produces/targets - closes need → binding → resource.

module.description: The concrete platform module/recipe that realizes the type in this environment.

profile.description: Optional resource-type profile this binding draws from (neutral/azure/aws/k8s/on-prem/openstack - the resource-type catalog).

params.description: Binding-time parameters passed to the module (conceptually merged over need `params` + environment `param_overlay`).

outputs.description: Outputs this binding exposes (host/port/connection-string/…). A field may be secret-flagged - a reference/flow marker only, never a value.

description.description: Optional human note on this binding.

binding_module.description: A concrete platform module/recipe reference with a pinned version (`version_pin` is carried; no generator consumes it in v2.7.7). Substrate-neutral: AVM is ONE realization vocabulary, not THE vocabulary - a Terraform registry module, a Helm chart, or an Ansible role are equally valid.

ref.description: Module/recipe locator - e.g. 'br/public:avm/res/db-for-postgre-sql/flexible-server', a Terraform registry path, a Helm chart, an Ansible role.

version_pin.description: Optional pinned module version (e.g. '1.2.3', '~> 4.0'). The continuous-readiness field (carried, unused this round).

system.description: Optional provisioner hint (free-text: bicep, terraform, helm, ansible, …). Free-text so on-prem systems fit; the authoritative IaC link is `resource.iac_refs`.

io_field.description: A typed input or output field of a resource-type contract or a binding. An output may be secret-flagged - a reference/flow marker only, never a secret VALUE. Mirrors the `io_field` shape in the resource-type profile schema (`profiles/infrastructure/`).

name.description: Field name (e.g. host, port, name, username, password, connection_string, endpoint).

type.description: Optional value-type hint (e.g. string, int, hostname, uri).

secret.description: When true this field is a secret - the model carries the reference/flow, never the value.

description.description: Optional description of the field.

resource_identity.description: The workload identity a resource runs as / authenticates with - named for the CONCERN, not the Azure product: a cloud managed identity (system/user-assigned), a Kubernetes or on-prem service account, or an AD service account. Semantic level only - mechanics live in the module.

kind.description: Identity kind, substrate-neutral: cloud system/user-assigned managed identity, a k8s service-account, an on-prem AD service account, or none.

name.description: Optional identity name/reference (a label, never a secret).

access_grant.description: An RBAC access triple: which identity may do what to which target. Substrate-neutral - a cloud IAM role assignment OR an on-prem AD/LDAP group grant. Semantic level only.

identity.description: The grantee identity (a `resource_identity` name, a group, or a principal label).

target.description: What the access is over (a resource, a scope, a data store - free-text/label; may be an IR###).

role.description: The role/permission granted (e.g. reader, contributor, db_datawriter, read-only).

observability_binding.description: Where this resource sends its telemetry - named for the concern (AVM calls this 'diagnostics'): logs and metrics sinks. Substrate-neutral: cloud diagnostic settings OR on-prem syslog/SNMP/Prometheus. Distinct from the quality-layer `observability` STRATEGY (product-wide); this is per-resource wiring.

logs_to.description: Log sink targets (e.g. a log-analytics workspace label, 'syslog://…', a Loki endpoint).

metrics_to.description: Metrics sink targets (e.g. a monitor workspace, a Prometheus endpoint, an SNMP collector).

redundancy.description: Availability-domain spread - named for the concern (AVM calls this 'zones'): the fault domains this resource is replicated across. Substrate-neutral: cloud availability zones/regions OR on-prem sites/racks.

domains.description: The availability/fault domains (e.g. ['zone-1','zone-2'] cloud, or ['dc-1','dc-2'] / ['rack-a','rack-b'] on-prem).

strategy.description: Optional spread strategy note (e.g. 'zone-redundant', 'active-active across sites').

encryption_key.description: Encryption-key posture - named for the concern (AVM calls this 'customer_managed_key'): a cloud KMS/Key-Vault key OR an on-prem HSM/Vault. Carries a key REFERENCE, never key material.

managed_by.description: Who manages the key: platform-managed, customer-managed (cloud KMS/Key-Vault), or self-hosted (on-prem HSM/Vault).

key_ref.description: Optional key reference/label (a vault path or key id - a reference, never the key material).

deployment_unit.description: Optional deployment-unit boundary (carried; no generator consumes it in v2.7.7): groups resources that deploy together and names the outputs the unit exports to other units.

unit_id.description: Logical deployment-unit id this resource belongs to (resources sharing a unit_id deploy together).

exported_outputs.description: Output names this unit exposes to other units (the cross-unit wiring boundary).
